### 1. apply-with-verify-cancelled-result-compensation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs:80-134` (the `RunWriteAsync` body of `ApplyWithVerify`) reads `preBaseline`/`postCheck` `CompileCheckDto` results but never inspects `.Cancelled`. `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompileCheckService.cs:56-62` shows `CheckAsync` catches `OperationCanceledException` internally and returns a normal (non-throwing) `CompileCheckDto` with `Cancelled=true` (field declared at `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/CompileCheckDto.cs:30`) instead of propagating the exception. Because `ApplyWithVerifyTool`'s existing `catch (OperationCanceledException)` block (lines 163-191) only fires when an exception actually escapes, a caller-token cancellation that lands *inside* `compileCheckService.CheckAsync` is currently invisible to the tool: (a) pre-apply cancellation — the tool proceeds to call `refactoringService.ApplyRefactoringAsync` anyway, applying a change the caller already cancelled; (b) post-apply cancellation — `newErrors` is computed from a partial/incomplete diagnostic list and the tool can return `status="applied"` (or `applied_with_errors`/`rolled_back`) for a verification pass that never actually completed, with zero best-effort revert attempted. Verified the existing `ApplyWithVerifyCancellationAndScopeTests.cs` does NOT cover this: its `FakeCompileCheck.OnCall` throws `OperationCanceledException` directly to simulate cancellation, a shape the REAL `CompileCheckService` never produces — so none of the 5 current tests exercise the actual production failure mode (a returned `Cancelled=true` DTO with no exception). No bundle candidates (`bundleCandidatePeers` empty) — Rule 1 n/a. |
| Approach | Single file: `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`. (1) Extract the existing `catch` block's revert logic into a private static helper `BestEffortRevertAfterCancellationAsync(IUndoService undoService, string workspaceId, ILogger? logger)` — reused by both the new checks and the existing catch block (pure DRY extraction, no behavior change to the catch path). (2) Immediately after computing `preBaseline` and before calling `refactoringService.ApplyRefactoringAsync`, add: `if (preBaseline.Cancelled) { c.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(); throw new OperationCanceledException(c); }` — zero apply calls, zero revert calls. (3) Inside the existing `try` block, immediately after computing `postCheck` and before the `newErrors` diff, add: `if (postCheck.Cancelled) { await BestEffortRevertAfterCancellationAsync(undoService, workspaceId, logger).ConfigureAwait(false); c.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(); throw new OperationCanceledException(c); }` — exactly one best-effort revert on a fresh `RevertBudget`-scoped token (mirrors the existing catch block's fresh-token pattern), then surface cancellation. (4) The existing `catch (OperationCanceledException)` block's OBSERVABLE behavior is unchanged — it still reverts on a fresh 30s-budget token, logs revert failure at Error, and rethrows the original caught exception; only its revert logic is now routed through the shared helper. |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`. Test files (1, modified/extended, not new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ApplyWithVerifyCancellationAndScopeTests.cs` — extend `FakeCompileCheck` with an optional "return a `Cancelled: true` DTO at call index N instead of throwing" mode, add 2 new `[TestMethod]`s (pre-apply-cancelled-DTO and post-apply-cancelled-DTO cases). No files deleted. No Rule 3/4 exemption needed — well under both caps. |

The non-cancelled `applied`/`applied_with_errors`/`rolled_back` paths must remain byte-identical — verified by the 3 existing `CompileCheck_*` project-scoping tests, whose `FakeCompileCheck` defaults `Cancelled` to `false`. |

Then `mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter ApplyWithVerifyCancellationAndScopeTests` covering all 7 methods (5 existing + 2 new): the 2 new tests must pin `FakeRefactoring.ApplyCalls`, `FakeUndo.RevertCalls`, and `FakeUndo.LastRevertToken.IsCancellationRequested` exactly as the existing thrown-cancellation tests do, and assert the thrown exception is `OperationCanceledException` carrying the caller's token. ### 2. undo-revert-preserve-snapshot-on-failure-or-cancellation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Both revert entry points consume undo state BEFORE the cancellable restore work confirms success, so a failed or cancelled restore permanently destroys the retry target. `UndoService.RevertAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/UndoService.cs:97-135`): line 99 unconditionally `_snapshots.TryRemove`s the pending snapshot, and lines 110-123 remove the matching `_history` entry, both BEFORE the actual restore runs at lines 127-134 (`RevertFromFileSnapshotsAsync` / `RevertFromSolutionSnapshotAsync`). If that restore throws `OperationCanceledException` or returns `false` (disk `IOException`/`UnauthorizedAccessException` inside `RevertFromFileSnapshotsAsync:300-307` or `PersistRevertChangesAsync:494-498`), the snapshot is already gone — confirmed live at the only two call sites that treat `RevertAsync` as a compensating retry: `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs:150` (message at line 160 tells the caller "rollback_failed... Inspect manually" with nothing left to retry) and the cancellation-recovery leg at `ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs:174` (a second failed attempt has no snapshot to fall back on). `UndoService.RevertBySequenceAsync` (`UndoService.cs:137-241`) has the identical shape: lines 202-213 ("Apply the revert. Drop history entry first so concurrent callers can't double-revert.") `historyList.RemoveAll` and CAS-remove the LIFO `_snapshots` entry BEFORE calling the restore at lines 215-223; a `revert-failed` result at lines 225-233 has already destroyed the history entry, so the sequence can never be retried and its position in the dependency-ordered history list (used by the conservative overlap check at lines 174-200) is permanently lost. Not a bundle — `bundleCandidatePeers` is empty. |
| Approach | Single file: `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/UndoService.cs`. (1) `RevertAsync`: replace the opening `_snapshots.TryRemove` with `_snapshots.TryGetValue` (peek, don't consume). Run the fast-path/legacy-path restore against the peeked snapshot first. Only when the restore returns `true` (or after it returns, not on a thrown cancellation) move the existing history-removal block (current lines 110-123) and consume the snapshot via the atomic CAS overload `_snapshots.TryRemove(new KeyValuePair<string, UndoSnapshot>(workspaceId, snapshot))` — this both satisfies "successful revert consumes exactly the intended snapshot once" and avoids clobbering a newer `CaptureBeforeApply` that may have landed while the restore was in flight. On a `false` return or a thrown `OperationCanceledException`, leave `_snapshots`/`_history` untouched so the same call is retryable. (2) `RevertBySequenceAsync`: keep the existing lookup (142-172) and dependency-block check (174-200) unmodified. Replace the unconditional drop-first block (202-213) with a claim step that records the removed history-list index via `historyList.FindIndex`/`RemoveAt` (instead of blind `RemoveAll`) and CAS-removes the LIFO `_snapshots` entry only if it matches — this preserves the existing "concurrent callers can't double-revert" guard. Run the restore. On success, the claim stands (current happy path, lines 235-240). On `reverted == false`, reinsert the history entry at the recorded index (`historyList.Insert(index, target)`, preserving sequence ordering for future dependency checks) and best-effort restore the LIFO snapshot with `_snapshots.TryAdd(workspaceId, target)` (won't overwrite a newer capture) before returning the existing `Reason: "revert-failed"` result. No interface (`IUndoService.cs`) or return-type changes — `RevertAsync`/`RevertBySequenceAsync` signatures are unchanged, so no caller updates are needed in `ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`, `UndoTools.cs`, or `EditService.cs`. |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/UndoService.cs`. Test files (1, extended with new methods): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/UndoServiceTests.cs`. No Rule 3 exemption needed (well under the 4-file cap). |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | (1) The `RevertBySequenceAsync` reinsert-on-failure path is new code with no prior precedent in this file — verify the reinserted index still points at the correct ordinal position when concurrent `CommitPendingCapture` calls have grown the list mid-revert (mitigate by re-deriving the insert position with a bounds check against current `historyList.Count`, already noted in Approach). (2) `_snapshots.TryAdd` after a failed sequence-revert is best-effort — if a newer `CaptureBeforeApply` raced in during the failed restore, the failed target will NOT be restored as the LIFO-pending snapshot (it remains retryable only via `RevertBySequenceAsync`, not plain `RevertAsync`/`revert_last_apply`); acceptable per Directive #6 (smallest complete fix) since the primary retry path for a sequence-targeted revert is itself sequence-targeted. (3) Verify `Clear(workspaceId)` (workspace-closed cleanup, line 521-525) still behaves correctly if invoked mid-revert — unaffected by this change since it clears both dictionaries unconditionally regardless of in-flight claims. (4) Fanout probe skipped — surgical reordering inside two existing methods, no signature/attribute/rename changes, no new callers to update. |
| Validation | Extend `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/UndoServiceTests.cs`: (a) `RevertAsync` restore-failure case — force `RevertFromFileSnapshotsAsync`'s disk write to fail (e.g. lock the target file exclusively or make it read-only before calling `RevertAsync`), assert the call returns `false`, then remove the obstruction and call `RevertAsync` again for the SAME workspace, asserting the retry now succeeds and restores the original content — proves the snapshot survived the first failure. (b) `RevertAsync` cancellation case — pass an already-cancelled `CancellationToken`, assert `OperationCanceledException` (or a graceful `false`, matching whatever the implementation settles on), then retry with `CancellationToken.None` and assert success. (c) `RevertAsync` happy-path consumption — after a successful revert, assert a second `RevertAsync` call for the same workspace returns `false` (snapshot consumed exactly once) and `GetLastOperation` returns `null`. (d) `RevertBySequenceAsync` restore-failure case with a later non-overlapping apply present — force the target sequence's restore to fail, assert `Reason: "revert-failed"`, then assert the target sequence is STILL retrievable/retryable via a follow-up `RevertBySequenceAsync` call for the same sequence number after clearing the obstruction, AND that the dependency-block check against the later apply still behaves correctly (ordering preserved). Keep the 3 existing tests (`RevertBySequence_NonOverlappingApplies_RestoresEarlierApply`, `RevertBySequence_LaterApplyOverlapsTargetFiles_DependencyBlocked`, `RevertBySequence_UnknownSequence_ReturnsUnknownSequenceReason`) green as ordinary-success/dependency/unknown-sequence regression coverage. Run `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` then `mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter "UndoServiceTests"` (also re-run `EditUndoIntegrationTests` and `ChangeTrackerTests` per the fixture's own doc-comment pairing) before falling back to `dotnet test --filter "UndoServiceTests"`. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness fix, no hot-path changes (revert is an infrequent, already-async operation; the change only reorders existing work, adding no new I/O or scans). |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | - **Fixed:** `UndoService.RevertAsync` and `RevertBySequenceAsync` no longer discard the undo snapshot/history entry before the restore completes — a cancelled or failed revert now leaves the same snapshot retryable instead of silently losing it, and `RevertBySequenceAsync` preserves dependency ordering across a failed-then-retried sequence revert. |

| Diagnosis | Three independently-maintained local type-enumeration walks, each with a distinct bug or shape defect, confirmed by direct read and `find_references` (each helper has exactly its 2 self-referencing call sites, no external callers): (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ImpactSweepService.cs:397-423` `NamespaceTypeEnumeration.GetAllTypes` — at line 412 `if (allowedKinds.HasValue && type.TypeKind != allowedKinds.Value) continue;` targets the OUTER `foreach (var member in ns.GetMembers())`, so a non-matching parent type skips its own `GetTypeMembers()` walk entirely (lines 414-418) — matching descendants nested beneath a non-matching parent are pruned and never yielded. Implementation: an explicit `Stack<IEnumerator<ISymbol>>` of enumerator frames — one frame per open container (`INamespaceSymbol.GetMembers()` or `INamedTypeSymbol.GetTypeMembers()`). Loop: `Peek` the top frame, `MoveNext()`; if exhausted, `Pop` and continue; on a namespace member, push its `GetMembers()` enumerator; on a named-type member, yield it iff `allowedKinds is null || type.TypeKind == allowedKinds.Value`, THEN unconditionally push `type.GetTypeMembers().Cast<ISymbol>().GetEnumerator()` as a new frame — descending regardless of whether the parent matched the filter (fixes bug 1's pruning) and recursing to arbitrary depth (fixes bugs 1 and 3's one-level cap). Aux storage is one `IEnumerator<ISymbol>` per open ancestor frame → O(tree depth), matching the Acceptance bullet. Order is pre-order depth-first matching `GetMembers()`/`GetTypeMembers()` declaration order (each container's subtree is fully exhausted via its own stacked frame before control returns to a shallower frame) — deterministic, matches the existing recursive semantics in (2). Migrate all three call sites and delete the local implementations: `ImpactSweepService.cs:140` and `:256` → `RoslynSymbolTraversal.EnumerateNamedTypes(compilation.GlobalNamespace, TypeKind.Class)`, delete `NamespaceTypeEnumeration` (lines 397-423); `CouplingAnalysisService.cs:58` → `RoslynSymbolTraversal.EnumerateNamedTypes(compilation.Assembly.GlobalNamespace)` (no filter — preserves current unfiltered-then-`ShouldAnalyze` behavior), delete `EnumerateDeclaredTypes`/`EnumerateNestedTypes` (lines 121-148); `SymbolSearchService.cs:144` → `RoslynSymbolTraversal.EnumerateNamedTypes(compilation.GlobalNamespace)`, delete local `EnumerateNamedTypes` (lines 211-227).
